## v2.4.3 "Touchstone" — what the synthesiser accepts, and what the licence requires

A touchstone is a stone you rub gold against; the streak it leaves tells you what
the metal actually is. This release settles the **two Fabric-plan risks that had
to be answered before any RTL exists** — and both were answered by evidence that
contradicted what the plan assumed.

RustyNES itself is unchanged. **The emulation core is untouched** — no behaviour
change to `rustynes-{cpu,ppu,apu,mappers,core}`, no new API, no dependency
movement. AccuracyCoin remains **141/141 (100.00%, RAM decoder)** and nestest
0-diff, run rather than assumed. The RTL and the synthesis run live in the
sibling `RustyNES_MiSTer` repository; this release is where the oracle records
the result, because the version line and the programme plan are RustyNES's.

---

### Risk 4 — the Quartus subset is FITTED, not documented

The plan called this the risk whose failure is **retroactive**. Quartus 17.0.2's
SystemVerilog subset is materially narrower than Verilator's, and a construct
rejected after ten thousand lines exist invalidates not one file but the style
every file was written in.

The acceptance criterion was never "it compiles". It was a fitted netlist **and
its resource report**, because only the second catches a 2 KiB memory that became
16,384 flip-flops — and Quartus does that **silently**, as a log warning, with
the build still succeeding.

Quartus Prime Lite **17.0.2 Build 602**, device **5CSEBA6U23I7** (the DE10-Nano
and SuperStation One part), defaults throughout — no `ramstyle` attribute, no
synthesis pragma:

```text
Analysis & Synthesis was successful. 0 errors, 0 warnings
Fitter was successful.               0 errors, 4 warnings

Total block memory bits  ; 16,384 / 5,662,720 ( < 1 % )
M10K blocks              ; 2 / 553
Total registers          ; 29
Logic utilization (ALMs) ; 17 / 41,910 ( < 1 % )
```

**29 registers, not 16,413.** The 2 KiB `logic [7:0] mem [0:2047]` inferred as two
M10K blocks from the *source style* alone. That was the whole gate.

Two findings it was not looking for:

- **The MIF column is populated** —
  `altsyncram ... Simple Dual Port ; 2048 ; 8 ; 16384 ; db/kitchen_sink.ram0_...`
  — so the `initial` block became a real memory-initialisation file. That is what
  makes a boot ROM land *inside* the block instead of being written at runtime.
  Documented behaviour, now observed.
- **The `enum` was recognised as a state machine** and one-hot encoded
  (`Encoding Type: One-Hot`), not flattened into anonymous logic.

**Zero synthesis warnings** is the stronger half of that first line: not merely
"no errors", but the synthesiser having nothing to say about any construct
present. The four fitter warnings are 58 unconstrained pin locations and a
missing `.sdc`, in a module with no pinout and no timing constraints — timing
closure is a rung-6 question.

**Nine constructs promoted to `fitted`. Three deliberately not.**
`kitchen_sink.sv` does not exercise plain `case`, `priority case` or `$bits`, so
those keep the *documented* status while their neighbours advance. Plain `case`
is near-certainly fine and `$bits` is an elaboration-time function — and
"near-certainly" is the word that document exists to refuse. Either extend the
kitchen sink and re-fit, or do not use them. No permitted construct failed, and
nothing moved to the forbidden table.

### Risk 1 — the `sys/` licence audit inverts the plan's own hedge

The plan required this **before any RTL is written**, because relicensing after
ten thousand lines exist is precisely the failure
`docs/originality-and-provenance.md` documents. Every file under
`Template_MiSTer`'s `sys/` was read and classified by its own grant, with comment
markers stripped and whitespace collapsed before matching.

| Classification | Files |
|---|---|
| GPL-2.0-or-later | 9 |
| **GPL-3.0-or-later** | **4** |
| GPL by reference, no version stated | 4 |
| Copyright, no grant | 4 |
| No header | 36 |
| **GPL-2.0-only** | **0** |
| | **57 total** |

The plan hedged that a GPL-2.0-**only** file would force the RTL *down* to
GPL-2.0-or-later. **There is no such file, and the binding constraint runs the
other way.**

Four files are GPL-3.0-or-later — `ddr_svc.sv`, `hps_io.sv`, `scandoubler.v`,
`sd_card.sv` — and **`hps_io.sv` is not optional**: it is how a MiSTer core
receives a ROM from the HPS and how the OSD reaches it. No core functions without
it. GPL-2.0-or-later may be combined into a GPL-3 work, because "or later"
permits the upgrade; GPL-3.0-or-later cannot be reduced to GPL-2.

So the combined bitstream **must** be GPL-3.0-or-later, which is already
RustyNES's licence. No relicensing is needed, and the hedge is inverted by
evidence rather than by argument.

---

### Fixed

**A stale success message in the RTL-subset policy checker.**
`check_rtl_subset.py` printed "the subset itself is unproven until
`quartus/synth.sh` produces a fitted netlist" on every green run. That was true
when written and is now false — and a success message describing a state the
project has left is how a check quietly stops meaning anything. It now names the
fit date and says that a construct added *since* then is what remains unproven.

### The install record, kept because it is reusable

Three findings that would each have cost an afternoon:

- **The tarball is a two-stage bundle.** `Quartus-lite-17.0.2.602-linux.tar`
  contains base **17.0.0.595** installers *and* a separate
  `QuartusSetup-17.0.2.602-linux.run` update, and the bundle's own `setup.sh`
  runs **only the base** — its last line is an `exec` on the 17.0.0 installer. A
  naive install lands on 17.0.0, which `synth.sh`'s `*17.0*` pattern would have
  waved through. The install script asserts `Version 17.0.2` exactly.
- **17.0 has no `--accept_eula`.** It arrived in 17.1, and an unknown flag is a
  hard error to a BitRock installer rather than a warning. Asking the binary
  `--help` is what caught it; copying an invocation written for a newer release
  is what would not have.
- **`--disable-components` takes device families by name**, so the install is
  scoped to Cyclone V and skips ModelSim (this programme simulates with
  Verilator), the GUI help and five unused families: **11 GB rather than roughly
  30**.

Also recorded: `download.altera.com` returns 403 to non-browser clients while
`downloads.intel.com` serves the same path; the installer hangs in
`do_select`/`futex_wait` *after* logging `Installation completed`; and bare `ldd`
reports 150–270 "not found" libraries that are Quartus's own, resolved at runtime
by the `bin/` wrapper scripts. All three look like failures and are not.

### Why 17.0.2 and not 25.1, checked rather than assumed

Quartus Prime Lite **25.1 does still support Cyclone V** — Lite is the only
edition that does, Pro having dropped the family — so device support is not what
rules it out. Three other things do: `Template_MiSTer`'s README pins **v17.0.x**
in writing; `sys/` is mandated verbatim and carries Platform Designer IP
generated under 17.0, which a newer Quartus will compile only after a **one-way
IP upgrade**; and a newer Quartus is the **more permissive** tool, so a pass
under 25.1 would report success for a property it never tested.

---

### Verification

- **AccuracyCoin 141/141 (100.00%, RAM decoder)**; nestest 0-diff. The core is
  untouched, but both were run.
- `quartus/synth.sh`: fit successful, 0 errors, 23 s elapsed.
- Sibling-repository CI green with every step reporting `success` — none skipped.

### Compatibility

Documentation and programme-record only on the RustyNES side. No save-state,
movie, netplay, or public-API change; `.rns` and `.rnm` are unchanged, and
`rustynes-cosim` remains excluded from the workspace and absent from the default
build.
